first.rationale: Current data shows activation down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Memory_91 demonstrates that activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first meaningful action—directly addressing the activation decline. Verifying memory_86 and memory_91 will confirm the magnitude of past lift from onboarding and activation interventions. While simplify_onboarding (memory_86) also shows promise, activation_messaging appears more directly targeted to the immediate problem (6% activation drop vs 4% onboarding drop). The competitive pricing pressure on SMBs is real, but promotional_pricing risks margin and doesn't address the engagement fundamentals. Activation_messaging can run as a standard experiment this week with quick feedback loop, preserving the option to pivot to pricing or onboarding simplification if results are weak. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is valuable but orthogonal to the SMB activation crisis. This approach maximizes sustainable revenue by fixing engagement first before committing margin to price competition.

mid.rationale: Archive verification confirms both memories are reliable. Memory_86 showed +13% completion lift and +3% retention. Memory_91 showed +6% activation lift and +11% week-one engagement with +1% retention. The activation decline (6% QoQ) is the more severe metric and memory_91's proven +6% activation lift directly counters it. Activation messaging also preserves retention (+1%) while addressing engagement fundamentals before committing to margin-eroding promotional pricing. Given the competitor's pricing pressure, fixing product engagement first strengthens long-term unit economics and positions us to compete on value rather than price. A standard_experiment scale allows rapid iteration if results underperform, preserving optionality for onboarding simplification or pricing intervention in subsequent cycles. This maximizes sustainable qualified revenue by addressing the root engagement problem rather than masking it with discounts.

final2.rationale: Circumstances have materially changed. Doubled churn conversations with price-sensitive SMBs indicate immediate revenue leakage that activation_messaging alone cannot arrest in the required timeframe. Memory_73 confirmed targeted promotional pricing is effective for price-sensitive SMB segments with strong acquisition and revenue lift. Memory_57 showed referral incentives worked in established customers without measurable retention harm. The competitive threat is now acute and existential to the SMB segment. Broad_rollout of targeted promotional pricing to at-risk SMB accounts is the only intervention with demonstrated efficacy that can stem immediate churn while we execute longer-term activation improvements in parallel. This preserves sustainable revenue by retaining the installed base, though it carries downstream margin risk and sets pricing expectations that may require sustained discounting. The alternative—allowing the SMB segment to churn to a competitor with superior entry pricing—is worse for long-term qualified revenue. Activation_messaging remains valuable but works on a longer horizon than the immediate churn crisis requires.
